title: Email delivery is a pluggable adapter behind a fixed contract
description: The blueprint owns a narrow email-delivery-adapter interface with a single send({ to, subject, textBody, htmlBody }) method returning a Promise resolving to a normalised outcome ({ ok, providerStatus, providerMessageId, error }). The project supplies the transport (SMTP, Resend, SES, a stub for tests). The magic-link routes call only the adapter interface; provider-specific fields, credentials, and rate-limit semantics never appear in the routes or the managers. Adapter-send failures are recorded on the event log and swallowed for the response body under the anti-enumeration budget.
rationale: Hard-coding a delivery provider ties the blueprint to a business decision the project owns; hard-coding provider errors into the response body reintroduces the enumeration oracle the anti-enumeration requirement closes. A narrow contract lets the project swap providers without touching auth code.
